verdict.rationale: ROS 2 supplies the building blocks for this. Its multi-language client libraries and CLI let code publish topics, call services and send action goals with feedback and cancellation to command a robot. SROS2/DDS-Security adds authenticated participants, encrypted traffic and per-enclave policies that work as scoped credentials. Nothing in the evidence shows an AI agent doing this, so a developer must hand-build the agent bridge and work through the security keystore setup. Missing for 10: any AI-agent-oriented integration or documented agent workflow, evidence of an end-to-end authenticated command path on a real robot, and independent or hands-on corroboration of security-scoped robot control.
